Signatures are produced at run time by a HARNESS STUB verifier over a per-JVM RSA keypair. Production verification is the JCA binding in :platform; these numbers certify :core's key selection and tamper detection, not the platform binding.
All key material is labelled TEST and is never written to eval/data/keys/.

Ring rotation date is fixed: one bundled key is inside the rotation window (uidai_test) and two are outside it, so a valid signature reports Valid and a valid signature under an expired key reports StaleKeys — distinguishable outcomes rather than the same code path. Every tamper arm is signed by the FRESH key precisely so the tamper check and the rotation check cannot be confused for one another.
Verdicts come from dev.kasoti.fusion.FusionEngine over findings produced by the real diary rules. No rule is reimplemented in the harness.

Baseline for every scenario: Track.PAPER_ID, quality CLEAN, math allChecksPassed=true and unexpired, macro MATCH at full margins with the clip used, face similarity 0.99 at full quality. PAPER_ID's load-bearing layers are quality/face/diary, so the coverage rules add nothing and the verdict reflects the diary alone.

R-ALIAS-01 is RED with `requiresSupervisorConfirmation`; FusionEngine reports `supervisorRequired`, so an AMBER script that reaches RED with the code present is still counted as a script miss rather than quietly accepted.
No clock is read: every crossing timestamp derives from 2026-09-01T09:00:00Z (AGENTS.md §5).

gates.name: MRZ mutate-catch
gates.detail: 10000 rows, seed 20260929, reference year 2026. 746 structurally blind rows are excluded from the denominator and reported separately as mrz.mutate_catch.structurally_blind. Source: EVAL.md §2 D-MRZ.

gates.name: MRZ false-positive rate on valid documents
gates.bar: 0% — EVAL.md §4 precision; not in SPEC.md §7, but a suite that passes the catch gate by flagging everything is not evidence
gates.detail: Valid rows are the corpus rows with mutation=NONE and no blind-spot reason.

gates.name: MRZ structurally blind cases
gates.bar: publish the count and the reasons — EVAL.md §4, and the reason the 100% gate cannot hide behind them
gates.observed: 746 of 10000 rows (7.46%): 746 x TD1 has no composite check digit: a recomputed field check digit is not detectable by MRZ arithmetic
gates.detail: These rows are undetectable by MRZ arithmetic. They are the substrate the other layers (QR signature, chip PA, macro, face) exist for, and no MRZ gate can close them. Full reasons are itemised in the table below.

gates.name: QR tamper-catch on rejected fixtures
gates.detail: bit-flipped payloads, re-encoded fields, rogue-key signatures and unsigned payloads, all of which must not verify. SecureQr reports a signed but unverifiable payload as UnknownKey (no key matched) and an unsigned one as Invalid; both are rejections, and RedRules.qrSignature collapses them into R-QR-01 behind a single signatureValid boolean.

gates.name: QR accept rate on genuine signed fixtures
gates.bar: 100% — refusing every payload satisfies the tamper gate and is useless
gates.detail: Genuine payloads signed by a bundled key must return SigResult.Valid.

gates.name: QR↔print cross-check catches a valid signature over the wrong person
gates.detail: A genuine, correctly signed payload compared against a mismatched printed name and DOB must produce at least one QrMismatch.

gates.name: Diary rules on planted D-SCEN scripts (verdict + finding codes)
gates.detail: Run through dev.kasoti.diary.{aliasRule,impossibleTravel,facilitatorRule} and dev.kasoti.fusion.FusionEngine — the product path, not a harness copy. Baseline: Track.PAPER_ID, quality CLEAN, math allChecksPassed=true and unexpired, macro MATCH at full margins with the clip used, face similarity 0.99 at full quality. PAPER_ID's load-bearing layers are quality/face/diary, so the coverage rules add nothing and the verdict reflects the diary alone.

gates.name: Diary rules stay GREEN on benign D-SCEN scripts
gates.bar: 100% — a rule that fires on an ordinary week will eventually accuse someone who did nothing
gates.detail: Benign scripts are ordinary multi-post weeks: one post and one cohort per crossing, 24 h apart, no alias, no watchlist.

gates.name: Diary 1:N rank-1 retrieval on a synthetic gallery
gates.observed: rank-1 100.00%, actionable 100.00% over 10 probes against 10001 distractors
gates.detail: The gallery is synthetic: %d distractors plus the true event, ranked by score. `actionable` additionally requires top − runner-up ≥ DELTA_MARGIN, because a rank-1 hit the runner-up nearly matches is not an identification.

gates.name: Unit parity: :core vs independently computed references
gates.detail: Reference values are computed in the harness from the published algorithms and the ICAO 9303 worked examples, not read from :core.

gates.name: Latency microbenchmark within host stage budgets
gates.bar: host advisory budgets — SPEC.md §7's 15 s ceiling is a DEVICE gate
gates.detail: Measured on the host JVM, not on a device. The device numbers EVAL.md §4 requires are produced by a device run of this same suite, with a build fingerprint recorded.

gates.name: Wall-clock stranger check on eval-host-jvm (NOT a NAMED device) [HOST — advisory]
gates.observed: not measured on a device — this host run is not a NAMED device
gates.detail: SPEC.md §7's 15 s stranger ceiling is a device gate. The host sum of stage p95s is median 12.70 s (p95 12.70 s, n=1), but a desktop JVM number is not a claim about a low-end phone, so this gate is SKIPPED rather than passed or failed. A device run of this suite produces the real measurement.

thresholdProvenance.name: FACILITATOR_MIN_GROUPS
thresholdProvenance.note: A-FAC-01: many crossings sharing at most this many distinct groups.

thresholdProvenance.name: T_ALIAS_HI
thresholdProvenance.note: R-ALIAS-01 needs supervisor confirmation on top of the similarity threshold; the threshold alone is not the rule.

thresholdProvenance.name: T_FACE_GREEN
thresholdProvenance.note: Shipped default 0.55. Same conflict as T_FACE_RED.

thresholdProvenance.name: T_FACE_RED
thresholdProvenance.note: Shipped default 0.35 is FUSION.md §5's 'TBD by tuning' placeholder, not a fitted value. NOTE: ThresholdName.T_FACE_RED.tuningDataRef reads 'D-FACE report split' — see the spec-conflict section of summary.md.

thresholdProvenance.name: T_WL
thresholdProvenance.note: A-WL-01 fires at any similarity at or above this value.

thresholdProvenance.name: VMAX
thresholdProvenance.note: 120 km/h, fixed by policy (FUSION.md §2 R-TRAV-01) and logged, not fitted. This is a policy value and is never a report-split tuning claim.
